note: Evaluated by the SHARED tools/gauntlet/tier1/check-witnesses.sh, called a second time with the journey transcript as its CONTEXT file. Tier 1's own witness set runs first against the same evidence with the bootstrap plan as context; the evaluator takes one context file, so two calls is the supported shape and forking it would not be. `plan-jq` therefore reads the TRANSCRIPT here.

witnesses.provenance: SPL Token and Token-2022 maintain `Mint.supply` as the sum of every token account's `amount`; the founding revokes the mint authority immediately after minting (SetAuthority MintTokens -> None), so the supply is frozen for the whole journey. The equality is therefore against the TOKEN PROGRAM's accounting, which is a second implementation the protocol does not control, and not against any dClutch belief. A dClutch defect that moved an atom into an account this journey does not name would leave the tracked sum short of a supply that did not change.

crates/dclutch-market-contract/src/market.rs: 'Each state cell owns one native claim. A complete set contains exactly one unit of every cell claim and is backed by one Hoard collateral atom.' The claim unit the law multiplies by is read from the Registry's published linked ProductBasisV3 record (`payout_scale`), NOT from the Hoard divided by the outstanding supply — deriving it from the founding poststate would make this assert that the founding equals itself.

The seven laws are stated in tools/gauntlet/journey/src/ledger.rs with their sources: L1/L2 against the token program's frozen supply, L3 against the Claims aggregate's own liability record versus the Positions it owes, L4 against the written complete-set invariant above, L5 against each stage's DECLARED delta stated before the stage runs, L6 against the rent a closed account carried, L7 against the fees the CHAIN charged summed off the stage's own transaction evidence. A law that cannot apply at a boundary records itself `inapplicable` with a reason and is counted, so this cannot go green by a law quietly ceasing to apply.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | startswith("journey: open and fund synthetic holder")) | select(.error == null)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: A cross-check between two independent derivations: the load knob the campaign was invoked with, carried in the transcript, against the chain's own count of finalized error-free transactions carrying that label. Neither side reads the other. A holder that failed to open, or a retry that opened two, moves one side and not the other.

The whole arc, pinned in one string. DCLTGMF1's commit-last stage is `open_series_market` (crates/dclutch-market-core-codec/src/generated.rs:922), which goes Founding+Prepaid -> Open+Consumed in ONE transition and never passes through Ready. That USED to be a dead end -- the only route creating the SourceResolutionStateV2 every terminal receipt consumes admitted Founding+Prepaid alone -- and the FIRST run of this tier reported exactly that, by reading the code. `edfcb24` admitted the second prestate and `60a2101` walked it against the compiled ELFs; the gate is now `resolution_fund_prestate_admissible` (programs/dclutch-core-sbf/src/resolution.rs:386). Then the SECOND run of this tier drove the ladder on a chain and found the Market had no key: its SourceMaterialV2 named its source spec, window spec and statistic spec by demo digests, and a finalized record lives at the hash of its own body, so it named records nobody could ever publish. With the graph compiled, this witness pins the end of the arc -- the Market this campaign founds now carries a real terminal receipt, minted from a real Pyth publication verified by a real Wormhole router.

The same gate read the other way. `resolution_fund_prestate_admissible` (programs/dclutch-core-sbf/src/resolution.rs:386) admits (Founding, Prepaid) as well as (Open, Consumed), and this campaign leaves exactly one Market of the first kind on the same ledger -- the canonical Found31 Market, which the atomic founding does not consume. This campaign resolves the FIRST kind and deliberately leaves the second untouched, so one ledger carries both a resolved Market and an unresolved admissible prestate -- which is what a campaign testing the failure walk, or a second resolution, needs and would otherwise have to found for itself. The witness pins that the prestate is really there, so the claim does not decay into a plan.

L7 is `payer_delta + fees + watched_growth == 0`, and it exists because the other six cannot state it: L1..L5 are about collateral ATOMS and say nothing about the lamport side of a route, and L6 only fires when a watched account CLOSES. Its fee term is never a prediction -- it is summed off each stage's own transaction evidence, so the law compares the chain against what the chain charged. A route that quietly debited whoever submitted it, or placed rent into an account nobody named, breaks this and nothing else.

The companion the violation count needs. L7 records `inapplicable` with a reason at boundaries it cannot evaluate -- the founding's lamports belong to the tier-1 producer, and a boundary that admits a watched label has no predecessor balance to difference against -- and a law that is inapplicable everywhere would satisfy the violation count while proving nothing at all. This pins that it HELD at least once, which is the difference between a law and a decoration.

A stage that refuses does not discard this campaign: the transcript and the complete conservation ledger are written first, the refusal is recorded on the stage AND here, and the run fails afterwards. That is deliberate -- a wall is worth more beside a complete ledger than as an error that throws the rest away -- and it means a green ledger is not by itself evidence that the journey got where it was going. This witness is the other half.
